newsitem.title: UK: EU sugar exports to Middle East seen falling 40 pct.
newsitem.headline: EU sugar exports to Middle East seen falling 40 pct.

text.p: Annual European Union (EU) sugar exports to the Middle East should fall by as much as 800,000 tonnes as three local refineries move to satisfy demand, a F.O. Licht analyst said on Thursday.
The sugar refineries in Dubai, Saudi Arabia and a third planned in Oman would severely hit EU exports to the region, said Licht's Christoph Berg at a two-day conference hosted by Agra Europe.
"While these refineries are certainly a boon for traditional raw sugar exporters like Australia and Thailand, the business of white sugar suppliers like the EU will get hurt badly," Berg said.
"We expect EU exports to this region to drop by around 40 percent to no more than 500,000 to 800,000 tonnes," he added.
The EU's high-quality white sugar represents the lion's share of exports to the Mideast Gulf countries, according to the International Sugar Organization (ISO).
Dubai's Al Khaleej refinery, which started production in late 1995, recently said production capacity was to be doubled to 700,000 tonnes this year.
Saudi Arabia's new refinery at Jeddah, which recently began operations with a start-up capacity of 500,000 tonnes, had an option to expand to 630,000, Berg said.
In Oman, a consortium of traders had initiated plans to build a 360,000-tonne capacity refinery, with commissioning scheduled for 1998.
"All this adds up to over 1.6 million tonnes of high quality white sugar capacity in one of the world's most important deficit regions," Berg said.
